findings.finding: The open data adds to $19.98 billion of capital for 2027 to 2030
findings.what_was_found: City open data nnnm-9sfh, fund = Capital, years 2027 to 2030: already approved $6,949.27 million + proposed $13,029.43 million = $19,978.70 million.

The City's budget page and news release give $21 billion over four years and do not say which rows that covers. The 2027 to 2030 rows round to $20 billion. findings.finding: Six business units where the business cases and the open data differ by more than $1 million
findings.what_was_found: 33 business units compared for 2027 to 2030; 27 match within $1 million. The six: City & Regional Planning +1.2; Downtown Strategy +31.5; Mobility +44.0; Project Development +31.1; Public Spaces Delivery -393.5; Recreation & Social Programs +283.9 ($ millions, business cases minus open data). They net to -1.8. The full table with every year is in section 1 of this report.

The differences equal specific requests, which is what would be seen if the open data files those requests under Public Spaces Delivery (the unit that builds) while the business cases list them under the unit that asks. Recreation & Social Programs: request 82 (GamePLAN - Wave 1 Projects), largest yearly gap $0.04 million; Downtown Strategy: request 219 (Downtown Streetscape and Public Realm Program), largest yearly gap $0.04 million; Mobility: request 57 (Major Road Reconstruction), largest yearly gap $0.14 million; Project Development: request 200 (Build Back Better - Pathways & Repaving) + request 201 (Calgary Pathway Program) + request 263 (Local Area Investment Fund), largest yearly gap $0.22 million. City & Regional Planning: the open data has nothing for 2027 and the cases have $1.165 million, the 2027 amount of request 193. The five differences add to $391.7 million against the $393.5 million shortfall under Public Spaces Delivery. The Project Development match is a combination of three requests, so it is weaker evidence. The City has published no mapping: this is an inference from matching amounts.

The "4-Year Capital Budget Consideration" totals of the 260 capital requests add to 13,051,480 thousand dollars ($13.051 billion). Their year columns add to 13,051,473; the 7 thousand difference is the City's own rounding inside individual requests (183 requests exact, 41 one thousand over, 34 one thousand under, 1 two over, 1 two under). Against the open data's proposed capital: $13,056.13 million including 2031, a difference of -4.65 million (0.04%). The City's own statement is $13 billion.

findings.finding: The four purposes of new capital
findings.what_was_found: Maintenance or replacement $5,529.5 million, growth $4,520.7 million, service enhancement $2,644.0 million, transformative $357.3 million; they add to $13,051.5 million. Each is a calculation (the screen labels it so): each request's total times the City's own percentage for the purpose. The four percentages of all 260 requests were read again with a third PDF reader: all agree and each set adds to 100. 116 requests have a single purpose; 144 are split by the City between purposes. The City publishes no dollar total by purpose to compare with.

Counted three ways that agree: the dataset (124 and 260); the pages of the PDF that carry the heading of each layout (124 carry "Budget proposal rationale:", 260 carry "Capital Funding Consideration ($000s)", 0 carry both); and case by case, each request's own pages carry exactly one of the two headings. No request is ambiguous between the two kinds.

findings.finding: Differences between the PDF reading methods
findings.what_was_found: Four ways of reading were used: pdftotext with page layout (the reader that makes the dataset; columns by character position), pypdf (row labels followed by their numbers), pdfplumber (numbers placed by position on the page) and pictures read by eye. The three text readers give exactly the same words on 736 of 792 pages (pdftotext and pdfplumber) and differ elsewhere only in how they split hyphenated words in sentences ("long-term"). They give the same numbers on 787 of 792 pages; the five pages that differ are three contents pages and two sentences of prose, none in a funding table. Details and limits are in section 2.

The data files are the site's own, so this needed someone able to change the site already; the screen now refuses any other kind of address. 15 of 15 checks pass.

findings.finding: No commercial proposal in the current files; the commercial opportunity is removed from the plan
findings.what_was_found: The commercial proposal file was never committed to the repository. At the owner's instruction of November 11 the commercial section, the related decision and the related wording were removed from the reports and from the review page that is kept outside the repository. A search of the documents, the new screen, its data, the new module and the two tools for ten words and phrases (commercial, pricing, price list, subscription, paid idea, paid tier, revenue-earning, earn revenue, monetiz, paywall) finds 13 lines, each listed with the reason it is there: 11 record the removal or state that the screen has no paywall or payment code, 2 are the City's own title of request 108 (about subscription-based software), and 0 are unexpected. The pages of this verification report, which discuss the removal, are not counted.
findings.how_to_repeat: grep -rniE "commercial|pricing|subscription|paid idea" docs/ ui/budget-intel* budget_intel.py tools/budget_intel_*

findings.finding: The branch's first commit still holds one sentence about paid ideas
findings.what_was_found: Commit 50acadc (the version the owner examined) contains, in two report files, one sentence listing kinds of paid service that were being considered and two mentions of "a product meant to earn revenue". No prices, no figures, no names. Later commits remove the text from the files but not from the history of this public branch. Two ways to close this, both the owner's decision: (a) at publication, merge the branch as a single squashed commit, so the sentence never enters main's history (recommended; nothing to do now); (b) rewrite the branch now as one commit and force-push it, which removes it from the branch as well. Not done without instruction, because rewriting history is not reversible.

In everything the branch adds: no e-mail address, no telephone number, no home or work address, no account name other than the public repository's, no path of the machine the work was done on and no session link in any file. Run records give only public run numbers and addresses. The owner is named only as the copyright holder already named on the site.

Every section was opened on four screen sizes in both themes (24 of 24 checks pass): each draws with content, nothing is wider than the screen, the page never scrolls sideways, no script error, no failed request. Screens: a 1440 by 900 desktop window, and emulated iPad Mini, iPhone 13 and a 360 by 640 phone.

7 of 7 checks pass on an emulated iPhone 13: the site menu opens; Budget Intelligence is under Money after City budget; tapping it opens the screen and closes the menu; each of the eleven sections opens from the strip of sections, stays in view and is kept in the address; the section buttons are at least 40 pixels each way; a link to one request opens that request.

8 of 8 checks pass. The expected numbers were worked out by the test from the data file, not typed in: every value of seven of the nine filters one at a time (40 values); the values of the other two (department, 13; reason given, 6) each cover all 384 requests exactly once; 20 combinations of kind, ward and Council priority, nine searches (words, a Budget ID, a number, nothing found), the totals line, and paging through all 384 requests in order.

5 of 5 checks pass: "Save this list" downloads a CSV of 384 rows; 25 columns of every row (9,600 cells) were compared with the data file and all agree, including dashes kept as blanks and the status "Proposed, not approved"; the capital totals add to 13,051,480 thousand; with filters on, only the filtered requests are exported; a title containing commas and quotation marks survives.

3 of 3 checks pass: all 384 rows link to the City's own PDF at that request's page number, in a new tab; inside an opened request every link goes to its page (13 requests tried). The City's file was downloaded again on November 11 and is the same file that was read (same checksum).

findings.finding: PDF links: does the document open at the right page on every device?
findings.what_was_found: The link ends in #page=N, which the PDF viewers of Chrome, Edge and Firefox follow. Some phone browsers open a PDF at its first page whatever the link says; that cannot be tested without the devices.
findings.how_to_repeat: On a phone, open a request and tap "p. 180"

findings.what_was_found: 5 of 5 checks pass: the site's own theme button switches the screen between light and dark and back; surfaces, text and the map change; charts and the map are still drawn; switching while on each of the eleven sections keeps the section drawn.

17 of 17 checks pass, after two defects found by this audit were fixed on the branch. Found: opening or closing a request, paging, and choosing a year each redrew the list and dropped the keyboard focus, so a keyboard user was sent back to the top; and the simulator's slider had no label a screen reader could read. Fixed: the focus now stays on the control that was used; the slider is labelled; and the section list now works as a radio group should (one Tab stop; arrow keys, Home and End).

findings.finding: Accessibility: what a scripted audit can check
findings.what_was_found: 19 of 19 checks pass in both themes on all eleven sections: every button, link and control has a readable name; every form control has a label; every table has header cells; headings do not skip a level; charts and pictures are named or marked as decoration; no repeated ids; text contrast is at least 4.5 to 1 (3 to 1 for large text) for every piece of text measured (3,372 in each theme, gradients included); pinch zoom is allowed; at 200% text size the page does not scroll sideways.

findings.finding: Accessibility: a full audit with a screen reader
findings.what_was_found: No screen reader (VoiceOver, TalkBack, NVDA) was run and no person who relies on one tried the screen. The scripted audit is hand-written for this screen; it is not a complete test against the accessibility guidelines.
findings.how_to_repeat: Try the screen with a screen reader; a short list of what to try is in section 5

findings.what_was_found: Every phone and tablet result above comes from an emulated device in desktop Chromium: the screen size, touch and browser name are imitated, but not the real browser engine (Safari on an iPhone), the real keyboard, or real download and PDF behaviour. No real device was available to this review, so no real-device result is reported. A ten-minute list for the owner to try on a phone is in section 5.
findings.evidence: evidence/ux/ux-results.json (every result names what it was tested on)
findings.how_to_repeat: Open the working preview (on the review page) on a phone and follow the list in section 5

findings.what_was_found: On the final files: all 27 screens (the 26 existing ones and the new one) open on a desktop window and an emulated phone, 54 of 54, with no script error and no failed request. Compared with the same test on main before development, the only screens whose content changed are the three that gained an entry: How it is counted (one note), Data Scientist (one topic) and Data Genie (one suggested question). 40 of 40 interaction checks pass. With each data file hidden in turn (7 cases) no section shows a script error and each says plainly what could not be loaded. The search defect that is already on the live site (an error if you type before the index has loaded) is still there and was not changed.

findings.finding: Data Genie and the Data Scientist can read the new data
findings.what_was_found: Tried the way the website runs them (the Python files it ships to the browser, with no site data folder): 23 of 23 checks pass. The dashboard tool answers for the new section with the same figures as the screen (384 requests; $13,051.5 million; 855 positions; the four purposes; the 17 part-requests), for one request by number, for lists by words, kind and ward, by department, Council priority, service area and ward, and for the checks; the method note is served; the Data Scientist has a topic for the budget requests; every answer carries the instruction to say proposed, not approved, to take no side, and never to divide a citywide amount.

findings.finding: A live conversation with Data Genie about the new data
findings.what_was_found: Not run: it needs the owner's access code and uses the owner's credits, and the assistants only run on the published site or the desktop app. What was verified is everything up to the assistant: the tool, its description, the data and the guidance it is given.
findings.how_to_repeat: After publication: ask Data Genie "What are the ten largest requests in the proposed 2027 to 2030 budget, and which page of the City's document is each on?"
